course_name_original: I.C. SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY OF MATERIALS AND BIOMATERIALS (TO0044)
course_name_en: I.C. Science and Technology of Materials and Biomaterials

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of basic knowledge of the chemical and physical properties of materials, of experimental methodologies for their characterization and of technical-professional skills for their selection for application purposes.

At the end of the course, the student will have to know the basic chemical principles underlying the properties of the different types of materials studied, their main properties and how they are related to their microstructure and / or chemical composition

The student must be able to apply the knowledge acquired by rationally evaluating the properties (mechanical, chemical, thermal, electrical, magnetic, optical) of the different materials and demonstrating the understanding of the chemical and microstructural basis of their behaviors.
The student must be able to evaluate, choosing among the various possibilities, the most suitable material for the production and / or design of various components depending on the final use.

The student must be able to describe, with language properties, the main characteristics of the different materials treated, and to effectively communicate the physical and chemical foundations underlying their properties.

syllabus_topics: Classification of materials: metallic, ceramic and polymeric
Other classification criteria: structural and functional materials, crystalline and amorphous
Properties of materials: mechanical, physical and chemical
Relationship between composition, structure and properties
Structure and properties of the diamond
Compact arrangements in plan and space
Point defects of physical and chemical nature
Role of point defects on the characteristics of some materials
Line defects: corner and screw dislocation
Mechanism of solidification of a metal
Elastic and plastic elementary behaviors and their interpretation on an atomic scale
Mechanical behavior in the presence of defects
Sliding mechanism of dislocation in a lattice
Role of dislocations and grain boundaries on the ductility of metals
Mentions on UNI and UNI EN standards
Examples of state diagrams of pure substance
Description of state diagrams under conditions of total miscibility and zero miscibility between solid phase components
Intermediate compounds with congruent and incongruent fusion
State diagrams in conditions of partial miscibility between solid phase components
Role of carbon on the strength of steels
Definition of steel and cast iron
Polymorphism of iron and solubility of C in Fe
Solid interstitial solutions: Ferrite and Austenite
Cooling of steels: equilibrium and non-equilibrium microstructures
Displacement transformation from Fe-γ to Fe-α
Martensite: formation mechanism and mechanical properties
Notes on the iron-cementite phase diagram
Notes on the production of steel by primary steelmaking
Cast iron and blast furnace slag
Mechanical treatments: obstacles to the movement of dislocations
Carbon steels and alloyed and unalloyed steels
Notes on corrosion: reaction mechanisms, factors that influence it, main forms of corrosion and protection methods
Characteristics and applications of stainless steels
Notes on cast irons: classification, strengths and weaknesses
Characteristics and main fields of application of non-ferrous metallic materials
Titanium and its alloys: characteristics and main fields of application
Raw materials: clays, thinners, fluxes, complementary materials
The structure of clays: tetrahedral and octahedral sheets
Forming techniques: pressing, extrusion and casting
Drying and firing: porous and compact paste ceramic
Definition, fields of application, production processes
Ceramic powders for ACM: characteristics and main production techniques (solid state reaction, fusion, vapor phase reaction, solution reaction)
Forming and compaction techniques: uniaxial pressing, isostatic pressing, inject molding, tape casting
Solid state sintering mechanism: two-sphere model
Mechanical and physical properties of ceramic materials
Theoretical and real resistance of MCs
Mechanical tests suitable for the characterization of an MC
Evaluation of the resistance of an MC in statistical terms: probability of breakage and survival
Introduction to glass and historical notes
Stabilizing and bleaching glass lattice modifiers
Characteristic points of glass: workability, softening, annealing and deformation
Composition and characteristics of some commercial glasses
Special glass: silica glass, boron and lead glass
Tempered glass: thermal and chemical hardening
The molecules of hydrocarbons: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes
The main functional groups of organic chemistry
Role of repeating units in the formation of polymeric macromolecules
The glass transition temperature of amorphous and semicrystalline polymers
Polymerization Mechanisms: chain polymerization and step polymerization
Examples of polymerization: polyamides, polyesters, phenolic resins, polyurethane
Physical and mechanical characteristics of polymers
Dependence of mechanical behavior on time and temperature
Fracture and fatigue in polymeric materials
Polymerization techniques: in mass, in solution, in suspension, in emulsion
Processing technologies: molding, extrusion, blowing and thermoforming
Production of polymeric fibers and films
Constituents of composite materials: matrix, reinforcement and interface
Classification of composites: based on reinforcement and matrix
Examples of composites with particles and laminates
Main polymeric matrices: epoxy and polyester
Composites with ceramic and metal matrix
Main types of fibers used as reinforcement
Glass fibers: chemical composition, characteristics and applications
Electrical properties of ceramic materials and polymers
Thermal conductivity and heat conduction mechanisms
Conduction of heat in metals, ceramics and polymers
Definition of optical properties of materials
Optical properties of non-metals: refraction, reflection, absorption, transmission
The types of magnetism: diamagnetism, paramagnetism, ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, ferrimagnetism
Magnetization and demagnetization of a ferromagnetic material

assessment_methods.method: Final partial test (written exam with multiple-choice questions, optional)

assessment_rules: The course includes an intermediate and a final partial test (optional) which, if passed (both of them), allow the total passing of the exam. The final test consists of a written exam based on multiple-choice questions concerning the topics of the course. Students with disabilities, specific learning disorders (SLD), or other special educational needs may receive individualized exam arrangements.
